findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting bypasses the $__range split guard
findings.body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` runs before `querySupportsSplitting`. `querySupportsSplitting` is designed to reject queries containing `$__range`/`$__range_ms` via `isQueryWithRangeVariable`, with a comment explaining these queries must not be split because the range variable would be interpreted relative to the split sub-range and produce an incorrect result. Since `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range`/`$__range_ms`, the check on the interpolated expr no longer sees them and will allow time-splitting of those queries. The range-variable check should be performed on the pre-interpolated expression or otherwise preserve the raw expression for this guard.

findings.title: Shard splitting applies template variables twice per query
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates every target with `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` at line 52. Later, `splitQueriesByStreamShard` sends each shard sub-request through `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which now also applies `applyTemplateVariables` to each target. Each query is interpolated again for every shard/time sub-request; the test change even asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called five times for a single target. If variable replacement is not idempotent (for example, a variable value contains `$` or template-variable syntax), the second pass can change the query incorrectly. One of the two layers should avoid re-interpolating already-interpolated targets.

findings.title: Queries can become empty after interpolation but are not re-filtered
findings.body: The target pipe filters `query.expr` before `applyTemplateVariables`. When a non-empty template expression such as `$var` resolves to an empty string, the query remains in `queries` and proceeds through partitioning. Since the interpolated empty expr is not a logs query, it is treated as a metric query and sent to Loki with `expr: ''`. Reorder the pipe to interpolate first and then `.filter((query) => query.expr)` so queries whose value is empty are skipped.
